title: arXiv AI weekly: 7 notable papers from 14–20 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart: this is an inferred ordering, and citation evidence for very recent work is limited.

method.citation_data: Semantic Scholar coverage incomplete; only one queried record returned, so citation counts were not used as a cross-paper ranking signal.
method.revision_coverage: The lastUpdatedDate query was rate-limited; updates of papers first submitted before the window may be absent.

sections.title: MCTS Is Counting the Wrong Thing: Learning Exploration Counts for LLM Reasoning
sections.abstract: The paper studies why standard MCTS can waste exploration across textually different but strategically similar reasoning branches, and proposes a learned count that shares evidence across related branches.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce Learned Pseudo-Count MCTS (LPC-MCTS), which estimates representation coverage with a lightweight Coin-Flipping Network and replaces exact UCT visit counts; they report gains over standard MCTS on five math and seven search benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evaluation is limited to those benchmark families and model configurations; transfer to broader, open-ended reasoning remains unestablished.

sections.title: Harnesses That Improve Themselves: A Unifying Framework for Self-Improving Agent Harnesses
sections.abstract: The paper frames an agent’s runtime harness as an editable part of the system and proposes a modular loop for diagnosing failures, changing harness code, validating changes, and deploying them.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors organize self-improving harnesses into four runtime components and a diagnose–patch–validate–deploy loop, and report that gated modular evolution beats prompt-only reflection and ungated full rewrites on their SWE-bench Lite setup at lower token cost.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper’s own experiments cover 60 Python bug-fixing tasks across two repositories, so the measured performance does not establish that the framework transfers to non-coding agents or long-term deployment.

sections.title: Groups of AI agents underuse resources despite shared evidence of increased capacity
sections.abstract: In controlled two-server simulations, the authors find that groups of language-model agents can leave capacity unused even after sharing evidence that a server has recovered, and test simple ways to spread requests.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that successful-request records help agents use a recovered server, while giving agents distinct numeric labels reduces synchronized demand and increases completed jobs in their simulated setting.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence comes from a controlled two-server simulation with a specific recovery and retry setup; it does not yet show that the intervention works in deployed, heterogeneous infrastructure.

sections.title: Visual Harness Scales General VLMs to Medical Images
sections.abstract: The paper presents a medical-image harness that lets general vision-language models inspect images iteratively, preserve evidence, check for omissions, and revise answers across multiple tasks and imaging modalities.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors’ VERA harness combines interactive visual tools, lossless evidence memory, an evidence map and verifier, and an iterative inspection loop; they report improvement on all 11 tasks for Qwen3.8-27B.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that evaluation uses public datasets, excludes real-world clinical validation, and uses smaller subsets for some API-model comparisons because of cost; they also cannot rule out training-data overlap for proprietary models.

sections.title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"
sections.abstract: The authors study counterfactual action outcomes under hidden disturbances and derive a first-order correction that reuses factual transitions to estimate what an alternative action would have done.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive an action-difference correction for JEPA world models under separated action and disturbance forces, prove an O(h^2) error bound under their assumptions, and report higher counterfactual prediction accuracy in their simulator experiments.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify failure cases at discontinuities, coordinate folds, and when disturbances scale the command; the reported experiments do not remove those assumption boundaries.

sections.title: Openhagen Worlds: Calibrated Environments for Measuring and Training Scientific Discovery Agents
sections.abstract: The paper introduces procedurally generated scientific-discovery environments with explicit scoring rules, hidden truths, budgeted experiments, and deterministic answer verification.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors contribute 27 environment families and 178 calibrated difficulty levels, with hidden-answer verification and controlled development/frontier splits; on 84 withheld frontier instances, the reported strongest model still trails the oracle.
sections.unique_caveat: These are procedurally generated benchmark environments, not evidence of improved performance in live scientific research; the paper reports that the largest remaining gap is in long campaigns of eight or more stages.

sections.title: Do Frontier Model Ingredients Add Up? A Replicated Factorial Study of Small Language Models
sections.abstract: The authors compare combinations of five language-model design and training changes under a shared data and compute budget, repeating selected runs with a second random seed.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that mixture-of-experts layers, Muon optimization, and a Gated DeltaNet hybrid produced the largest gains in their small-model setting, while most tested gains combined and some interactions persisted across two seeds.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors limit the conclusion to their small-model training setup and note that the expert models have greater total capacity; two seeds do not establish broad robustness of component rankings.
